body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته، أما بعد فإن الله تعالى أنزل القرآن على محمد (ص) بلسان عربي مبين، وقد جاء به جبريل عليه السلام إلى رسول الله (ص) منجما في ثلاث وعشرين سنة، ينزل بحسب الوقائع وبحسب ما يسأل عنه أهل الأرض وكان ذلك اتصالا بين أهل السماء وأهل الأرض، وارتباطا بين الخلق والخالق، جل وعلا ببيان ما يريده منهم وتشريع ما يرتضيه لهم، وقد ختم الله الرسائل إلى أهل الأرض برسالة محمد (ص)، وختم الكتب المنزلة إلى أهل الأرض بالقرآن، وجعله مصدقا لما بين يديه من الحق ومهيمنا على كل الكتب وناسخا لها..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: God Most High sent down the Qur'an upon Muhammad, upon whom be peace, in a clear Arabic tongue. Gabriel, peace be upon him, brought it to the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, in instalments over twenty-three years, coming down according to the events and according to what the people of the earth asked about. That was a communication between the people of heaven and the people of the earth, and a bond between the creation and the Creator, mighty and exalted, by the making clear of what He wants from them and the legislating of what He approves for them. God sealed the messages to the people of the earth with the message of Muhammad, upon whom be peace, and sealed the books sent down to the people of the earth with the Qur'an, and made it confirming the truth that was before it, and a guardian over all the books, and abrogating them..

flags.context: the description of the Qur'an's relation to the earlier scriptures
options: a guardian over all the books
a watcher over all the books
having authority over all the books
flags.note: Muhaymin is the word used of the Qur'an at Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:48, and the Sheikh is echoing that verse without quoting it, so the English should echo a standard rendering of it. The exegetes gloss muhaymin variously as guardian, witness and judge over the earlier scriptures, and the Sheikh does not choose among them. Option 2 picks one of the glosses and states it as the meaning.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on the Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, Ibn al-Jazari's versified primer on the rules of Qur'anic recitation. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 641–646 and the part numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the number in the title, not by id.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'In instalments' renders munajjaman — the revelation of the Qur'an piece by piece rather than in one act, which is the sense the Sheikh then unfolds in the following clause.
'According to the events' renders bi-ḥasab al-waqāʾiʿ, the occasions of revelation (asbāb al-nuzūl), though the Sheikh does not name the discipline here.
This record is the general introduction to the course and does not yet reach the text of al-Jazariyyah itself.
